questions.stem: On a velocity-time graph, an object's velocity increases uniformly from 0 to 20 m/s in 10 seconds. What is the acceleration?
questions.explanation: On a velocity-time graph, the gradient equals the acceleration. Gradient = change in velocity / change in time = (20 - 0) / 10 = 2 m/s². Option (d) multiplies velocity by time. Option (a) divides time by velocity. Remember: gradient of a v-t graph = acceleration.

questions.stem: A velocity-time graph shows a horizontal line at 15 m/s for 8 seconds. What is the displacement during this time?
questions.explanation: The area under a velocity-time graph equals the displacement. For a horizontal line (rectangle): area = velocity × time = 15 × 8 = 120 m. Option (a) divides velocity by time. Option (c) divides the correct answer by 2, as if it were a triangle — but a horizontal line forms a rectangle, not a triangle.

questions.stem: On a velocity-time graph, what does a straight line sloping downward from left to right indicate?

options.text: The object is decelerating (velocity is decreasing)

questions.explanation: A downward-sloping line means velocity is decreasing over time — the object is decelerating. The gradient is negative, indicating negative acceleration. Option (a) is incorrect because the object is still moving forward (velocity is positive but decreasing). The object only moves backward when the line goes below the time axis.

questions.stem: A car accelerates uniformly from rest to 30 m/s in 6 seconds. What displacement does the car cover? (Hint: find the area of the triangle on the v-t graph.)
questions.explanation: The area under the v-t graph is a triangle: area = 0.5 × base × height = 0.5 × 6 × 30 = 90 m. Option (c) of 180 m forgets the factor of 0.5 (calculates 6 × 30). This is a common error — when accelerating from rest, the v-t graph is a triangle, not a rectangle, so you must halve the product.

questions.stem: A velocity-time graph shows an object at +10 m/s that crosses the time axis and reaches -10 m/s. What has happened?

options.text: The object has slowed down and then sped up in the same direction
The object has changed direction and is now moving in the opposite direction
The object has doubled its speed

questions.explanation: When a velocity-time graph crosses the time axis, the velocity changes sign, meaning the object has changed direction. At the crossing point, the object is momentarily stationary (v = 0). Negative velocity means motion in the opposite direction to the positive direction. It has not stopped — it is moving at 10 m/s, but in the opposite direction.
